stubsObserved.evidence: /* The account, kept on this device. Nothing here talks to a server yet ... held in the browser so the whole app can be walked through. */
stubsObserved.standsInFor: account and wish persistence (reads and writes of drafts)
stubsObserved.consequence: Every read and write on these screens is localStorage 'fw-account'; no draft exists server-side, so a draft is invisible on another device (the 'not here' state).
Save is synchronous and cannot fail except by quota; debounce is 300ms (Maker.tsx:65); there is no network failure path to design for.

stubsObserved.evidence: const KEY = 'fw-maker'; readNote/writeNote on localStorage keyed by wish id
stubsObserved.standsInFor: per-draft metadata (given/chosen flags, wedding date, now, voice seconds) that the Wish type has no field for
stubsObserved.consequence: This state is never in the account object, so it would not reach a server if only the Wish were synced.

stubsObserved.evidence: let known: Account | null | undefined; (module cache of the account for this visit)
stubsObserved.consequence: Makes the loading state effectively unreachable after first read.
Draft ids are 8 char client random strings; server must issue ids or accept/replace them.

stubsObserved.evidence: wedding: string; // a Wedding's day ... the seal counts down to it
stubsObserved.standsInFor: a wedding date on the wish
stubsObserved.consequence: The date a countdown depends on is only in browser note storage, never on the Wish; the server must store it as a date plus the receiver's IANA zone (conventions) and compute countdown itself.
Duplicate formatted-string copy goes stale if the date changes while details is empty, and is locale/year dependent.
